answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a ferrous stake, a small time-locked bond of real value, before it may earn. One thread of work then maps to one bonded identity, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents recover the stake plus a share of fees, like bees carrying nectar back to the hive, while detected fakes forfeit theirs. The cost scales linearly with the attack, so mass fakery stops paying for itself.
